name: Credentialed participation
definition: Credentialed participation uses credentials to prove eligibility to take part in a process—without necessarily revealing full identity.
challenges: Eligibility verification often leads to excess data collection, creating surveillance and breach risks. Interoperability is hard: multiple agencies and partners may use incompatible standards, and revocation or status checking becomes complex. If the credential system is not well governed, it can enable exclusion, discrimination, or fraud at scale.
opportunities: Ethereum can serve as a neutral trust layer for credential status registries, revocation registries, or attestation anchors—supporting cross-organization verification without centralized control. Selective disclosure and ZK approaches can prove eligibility (e.g. age bracket, residency, membership) without revealing identity or additional attributes. Public-sector ecosystems like EBSI show how governments explore verifiable credential infrastructures for public services.
